put.summary: Import assets from a CSV file.
put.description:
Import annotations and applications from the given CSV file. 
The format of the CSV file is following: 
``` 
                     ,                       , <Annotation Type>  [, <Annotation Type>  ...] [, Application]   [, Tenant]   [, Line_Of_Business]   [, Business_Unit]   [, Project] 
<Object Type Value 1>, <Object Name or Key 1>, <Annotation Value> [, <Annotation Value> ...] [, <Application>] [, <Tenant>] [, <Line_Of_Business>] [, <Business_Unit>] [, <Project>] 
<Object Type Value 2>, <Object Name or Key 2>, <Annotation Value> [, <Annotation Value> ...] [, <Application>] [, <Tenant>] [, <Line_Of_Business>] [, <Business_Unit>] [, <Project>] 
<Object Type Value 3>, <Object Name or Key 3>, <Annotation Value> [, <Annotation Value> ...] [, <Application>] [, <Tenant>] [, <Line_Of_Business>] [, <Business_Unit>] [, <Project>] 
... 
<Object Type Value N>, <Object Name or Key N>, <Annotation Value> [, <Annotation Value> ...] [, <Application>] [, <Tenant>] [, <Line_Of_Business>] [, <Business_Unit>] [, <Project>] 
``` 
--- 
If an annotation value is empty then that annotation is removed from the object and inherited annotations are not affected. Date type annotation values must be passed in as unix time in milliseconds. When annotating volumes or internal volumes the object name is a combination of storage name and volume name using the "->" separator e.g. <Storage Name>-><Volume Name>. If an object name contains a comma, the whole name must be in double quotes e.g. "NetApp1,NetApp2"->023F. When annotating storages, switches and ports, 'Application' column will be ignored. Tenant, Line_Of_Business, Business_Unit, Project makes a business entity, any of the values can be left empty. 
 
 
The following object types can be annotated :
``` 
TYPE                           NAME OR KEY

1. Host                        id-><id> or <Name> or <IP>
2. VM                          id-><id> or <Name>
3. StoragePool                 id-><id> or <Storage Name>-><Storage Pool Name>
4. InternalVolume              id-><id> or <Storage Name>-><Internal Volume Name>
5. Volume                      id-><id> or <Storage Name>-><Volume Name>
6. Storage                     id-><id> or <Name> or <IP>
7. StorageNode                 id-><id> or <Storage Name>-><Storage Node Name>
8. Switch                      id-><id> or <Name> or <IP>
9. Port                        id-><id> or <WWN>
10. Qtree                      id-><id> or <Storage Name>-><Internal Volume Name>-><Qtree Name/Qtree simple Name>
11. Share                      id-><id> or <Storage Name>-><Internal Volume Name>-><Share Name>-><Protocol>-><Qtree Name/Qtree simple Name
                               (optional in case of default Qtree)>
12. Quota                      id-><id> or <Storage Name>-><Internal Volume Name>-><Qtree Name/Qtree simple Name>-><Quota Name>
13. Disk                       id-><id> or <Storage Name>-><Disk Name>
14. StorageVM                  id-><id> or <Storage Name>-><StorageVM Name>
15. VMDK                       id-><id> or <VM Name>-><VMDK Name>
16. DataStore                  id-><id> or <DataStore Name>
``` 
--- 
Examples of the CSV files: 

a) Adding an application and a business entity (N/A.N/A.Corporate IT.N/A) to a host and virtual machine 
``` 
, , Application, Business_Unit 
Host, 12.23.45.67, ERP, Corporate IT 
VM, id->780975491767428698, Sales, Dev Ops 
``` 
b) Adding 'Tier' annotation on volumes and internal volumes 
``` 
, , Tier 
Volume, Sym123445->023F, Gold 
Volume, Sym123445->012A, Gold 
InternalVolume, Sym1234555->INT1, Silver 
InternalVolume, id->1076, Bronze 
``` 
c) Removing application from volumes 
``` 
, , Application 
Volume, Sym123445->023F, 
Volume, id->1076, 
``` 
 
--- 
Note: When no valid Application Priority is specified, then the Application Priority defaults to: 
- Medium when an Application is created. 
- Previous Application Priority when an existing Application is updated. 
 
Application Priority is undefined when: 
  - No Application_Priority column is defined 
  - Application_Priority column is defined, but cell value is empty 
  - Application_Priority column is defined, cell value is non-empty, but contains an unrecognized priority

requestBody.description:
Request body could include expression, from/to time or timeRange, offset, timezoneOffset, field to sort, fields to include in file, and limit of total record counts.
  • expression: Optional.
  • timezoneOffset: Optional. Accept format of GMT<+|-><0:00 - 11:59>: GMT+0:30. Default: UTC.
  • sort: Optional. The name of the field to sort on prefixed by + or - to denote ascending or descending.
  • timeRange: Optional. When toTime is given, the timeRange will not be honored. Default: ONE_DAY.
  • fromTime: Optional. Must be no less than 0.
  • toTime: Optional. Default: the timestamp of "now".
  • fields: Optional. Array of fields to be included in the exported CSV file. Default: all available fields.
Time range calculation rules for different time parameters combinations are as below, and will return an error if time range is over 31 days after calculation:
  • fromTime, toTime, timeRange: fromTime and toTime will be used, and timeRange will be ignored.
  • fromTime, toTime: both will be used.
  • fromTime, timeRange: timeRange will be ignored and toTime will be considered as of "now".
  • toTime, timeRange: the timeRange will be replaced by ONE_DAY counted back from toTime.
  • toTime only: timeRange will be counted as ONE_DAY back from toTime.
  • fromTime only: toTime will be considered as of "now" and used.
  • timeRange only: the timeRange is counted back from "now".

  • toTime: Optional. Default: the timestamp of "now".
Time range calculation rules for different time parameters combinations are as below:
  • fromTime, toTime, timeRange: fromTime and toTime will be used, and timeRange will be ignored.
  • fromTime, toTime: both will be used.
  • fromTime, timeRange: timeRange will be ignored and toTime will be considered as of "now".
  • toTime, timeRange: the timeRange will be replaced by ONE_DAY counted back from toTime.
  • toTime only: timeRange will be counted as ONE_DAY back from toTime.
  • fromTime only: toTime will be considered as of "now" and used.
  • timeRange only: the timeRange is counted back from "now".
